newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sounds alarm on student drug abuse.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sounds alarm on student drug abuse.

text.p: International heroin traffickers have found a huge and growing market among Vietnam's school children and college students, a senior anti-drug squad official said on Monday.

"We have known about drug abuse in schools and universities for some years," said Vu Hung Vuong, deputy chief of staff at the police department's inter-ministry anti-drug programme steering board. "But it is now reaching alarming proportions."
Vuong told the daily Vietnam News in an interview that a survey finding that 1,006 pupils and university students had used drugs in the past two months showed just the tip of the iceberg.

"This figure was the result of an initial investigation in 26 of the 61 nationwide cities and provinces," he said. "The other 35...said that they had not yet found pupils and university students using drugs, but I think they may not have been doing their best."

According to police reports, high-purity heroin is being plied to students by food hawkers and others, often immediately outside school and college gates. Typically it is mixed in cakes and drinks or sold in tiny paper 20-milligram packages.

The United Nations Drug Control Programme, which believes heroin traffickers are targetting Vietnam's children in a bid to create a new market in one of East Asia's most densely populated countries, says packages are sold for as little as $2.70 each.
"Heroin sellers have found a large consumer market in our educational institutions, with many students easily convinced about the need to use drugs," Vuong said.
He said the authorities should pay more attention to educational programmes to warn against drug abuse and also introduce harsher penalties for offenders.

In the first eight months of last year more heroin was seized than in the whole of 1995 and the number of drug offences was up 13 percent from the same period in 1995, with 70 percent of those arrested under 30 years old.
